items.description: IT之家 11 月 27 日消息，韩媒 Economy Tribune 当地时间今日爆料称， Google（谷歌）计划为其第 10 代 TPU 芯片配备 512GB 的定制 HBM5 内存 。 谷歌 TPU 是当前最主要的 AI ASIC 产品，其规格可作为窥视未来 AI 芯片竞争的窗口。 从各位消息人士的近期泄露来看， TPU 10 当下指的是代号 "Quillfish" 的项目 ，预计由联发科技 (MediaTek) 负责设计服务工作，有望继续采用 Intel（英特尔）的 EMIB-T 先进封装，量产时间点落在 2029 年。由于还有约 3 年的时间，一切情况都可能发生变化。 谷歌近期在原版 TPU 8 系列的基础上推出 8tx、8i Max 两款芯片。此次更新并未在裸片的层面进行调整，而是通过封装集成、系统设计扩展了原有产品的边界。 参考 https://www.economytribune.co.kr/news/articleView.html ?idxno=3904543

items.description: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as the U.S. tightens its push to keep AI chips out of China.

items.content: Nvidia is under pressure to do things differently, and a new WSJ report shows how far that’s going. As for why those countries, Chinese companies have been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers there, a loophole the US Commerce Department closed — reportedly grudgingly —  earlier this month. items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn’t a virtue
items.description: On the same day that Anthropic entered the public market, a painstakingly human video game became one of most successful entertainment launches of all time.
items.author: Amanda Silberling
items.content: It should have been impossible for “Grand Theft Auto VI” (GTA VI) to live up to the hype. Fans waited 13 years for the newest installment in the crime-adventure franchise, and Rockstar Games exceeded even those inconceivable expectations when the game finally came out last week. GTA VI launched as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and made $3.79 billion on release day to mark what could be the biggest entertainment event ever – more massive than “Avengers: Endgame” ( $2.9 billion ) or Taylor Swift’s Eras tour ( $2 billion ). The 13-year wait certainly fueled the frenzy, and sales, around GTA VI, but some fans craved GTA VI because of what it represents in the emerging era of AI. Even the biggest workaholics among us – startup founders – scheduled time off to play the game, including Spiry co-founder Dima Beseda , who told TechCrunch, “I reshuffled my workload to free up time around the weekends and even booked vitamin IV drips to keep my energy up.” Yet some players felt a sense of anticipatory nostalgia as they wiped away a layer of dust on their Xbox to play the game they’d been looking forward to since they were kids. “We do have a view that GTA is likely to be the last game of its kind to be made this way,” Ben Feder , managing partner at TIRTA Ventures and former CEO of Rockstar parent company Take-Two Interactive, told TechCrunch.

items.title: S&P considers Nvidia credit downgrade over governance and ‘key man’ risks
items.description: The credit rating agency may lower Nvidia's credit rating to AA-, the fourth-highest rating.
items.author: Marina Temkin
items.content: S&P Global Ratings, one of the three major credit rating agencies, is considering downgrading Nvidia’s rating, citing concerns about the company’s management and governance practices. Despite Nvidia’s strong financial performance, the ouster and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang has raised concerns about “weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning” and “key man risk,” meaning heavy reliance on Huang for its future success, S&P said in a statement . The agency expects to finish its review within 90 days and could cut Nvidia’s rating from AA to AA-, the fourth-highest on its scale. Although Nvidia is certain to keep its investment-grade rating, a downgrade could raise its borrowing costs. Because Nvidia backstops neoclouds and other infrastructure companies that lack strong credit on their own, a lower rating could make their debt costlier or force them to post more collateral. In August, Nvidia announced plans to arrange $500 billion in financing for AI infrastructure with six financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs, Apollo, and Blackstone. Under the original terms, Nvidia would guarantee 25% of the loans. But even before Huang’s ouster and return, lenders had been demanding that Nvidia guarantee more, Bloomberg reported . A downgrade would likely prompt lenders to demand even larger guarantees.

items.title: OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work

items.content: OpenAI has started rolling out a unified Chat and Work experience in ChatGPT to a few of its users, amid criticism from some subscribers that the merger could restrict their usage. The ChatGPT maker began introducing the update to a small group of Pro subscribers, product lead Thibault “Tibo” Sottiaux said in a post on X on Tuesday. The rollout follows OpenAI’s earlier announcement of the merger in an email to users. An OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch that while most users are not expected to face more frequent usage resets, a small fraction of its heaviest users may hit their limits sooner. That’s among the concerns raised by some ChatGPT subscribers on social media and OpenAI’s community forum recently. The users fear that merging the usage limits for Chat and Work could leave them with less access to advanced reasoning models than they currently have, even as they continue paying the same subscription fees . Under the new system, Chat and Work will share a single usage meter across ChatGPT, the OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch. Conversations using the Instant model will, however, remain unlimited and will not count toward the shared allowance. Users can also continue using Instant after exhausting their usage limits. The spokesperson added that OpenAI would continue working to improve efficiency so subscribers could get more out of their plans. items.title: Jensen Huang broke Nvidia’s code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it
items.description: Most codes of conduct serve as a reflection of corporate culture. In Nvidia's case, that could have consequences.
items.author: Russell Brandom
items.content: When Jensen Huang gave his first all-hands address since returning as CEO, there was an odd emphasis on Nvidia’s code of conduct. He admitted to violating the code, then emphasized that no one was exempt from it. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” Huang said, according to Wired . “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” still matter. In other words, the code applies to everyone, but breaking it doesn’t automatically cost anyone their job, including, apparently, the CEO. It’s an awkward stance for a company whose CEO has admitted to breaking its rules. A central part of modern human resources, a code of conduct can seem like a quasi-legal rulebook that lays out unacceptable behavior. But experts say most codes are better understood as a reflection of corporate culture. When an infraction goes unpunished, the main risk isn’t legal but cultural — that employees will feel embarrassed or even angry about the company they work for. That’s the risk Huang now faces at Nvidia. items.description: Amazon and Meta are discussing a potential deal that would end a two-month-long blockade of Muse.
items.author: Lauren Forristal
items.content: Amazon may be having a change of heart about Meta’s AI agent, Muse. The two tech giants are reportedly discussing a potential deal that would allow Meta’s popular AI agent to connect directly to Amazon’s store. The talks would mark a significant reversal from just two months ago, when Muse users discovered they were unable to purchase products on Amazon and instead received an error message when attempting to check out. According to a Wednesday report by Fortune , citing people familiar with the discussions, Amazon and Meta have held multiple rounds of talks about the matter. Two key issues remain under negotiation: how search results would be presented and how advertising would be handled under a potential agreement. One of Amazon’s biggest concerns is how third-party shopping agents like Muse could affect its advertising business. In October, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy argued that few customers were making purchases through outside shopping agents. Amazon may also have been waiting for Muse to mature before agreeing to integrate it with its marketplace. If Muse places the wrong order or creates a problem with a purchase, Amazon could ultimately be left dealing with frustrated customers and unhappy sellers. Fortune reported that executives are concerned that third-party shopping agents could weaken Amazon’s direct relationship with consumers, according to people familiar with the matter.

items.description: The Nvidia founder apologized to his staff on Tuesday and said he was grateful for a second chance to lead the company.

items.content: After a whirlwind period during which Jensen Huang’s life fell apart and then came back together again, the Nvidia founder now wants his staff to know that he’s a changed man. Huang held Nvidia’s first all-hands meeting on Tuesday since his reinstatement on Monday. Huang emphasized that the code of conduct was still in effect, but that mitigating circumstances would matter a lot. items.author: Lauren Forristal
items.content: Shopping with AI is becoming less of a futuristic idea and more of something companies expect us to do. Walmart is the latest retailer making that shift, teaming up with Meta to let customers shop its Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent. The partnership, announced Tuesday, gives shoppers another way to find products, compare prices, and make purchases without browsing Walmart’s website themselves. Instead, customers can simply tell Muse what they are looking for and let the AI do the work. The announcement highlights how differently Walmart and Amazon are approaching AI shopping. While Amazon has taken steps to stop third-party AI agents from making purchases for customers, Walmart is leaning into the idea. To get started, users open the Muse app, sign in to their Walmart account, and return to the assistant to begin shopping. They can ask it to find specific products, compare options, or track down deals. Once a customer makes a request in Muse, the assistant sends it to Walmart, which returns relevant products and helps build a shopping cart. Walmart says it has built privacy protections into the experience. For instance, Muse doesn’t get access to a customer’s Walmart shopping history or other personal information. Shoppers can also set spending limits, require approval before purchases, and review orders placed by the agent. Plus, the company notes users can always delete their agent’s profile if they want to.

The idea of trust is Maple’s larger theme, as the startup proposes that there’s a way to build an AI app where consumers don’t have to trade privacy for convenience, as its competitors often require with their invasive privacy policies and data collection practices , and sometimes even training on users’ personal data . Instead of asking users to trust that Maple won’t misuse their personal data, it’s attempting to build a business where it can’t access that data in the first place. items.content: Anthropic’s stock fell below its IPO price of $83 , trading as low as $76 a share by midday Tuesday, down nearly 12% from Monday’s close. Falling below the IPO price is often seen as a negative signal because underwriters typically price offerings at a discount to their expected trading value. The AI industry has been eagerly watching how Anthropic’s shares trade, with VCs and other observers saying its performance could serve as a barometer for how public market investors value the sector. The dramatic slump comes less than a week after Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq at $111.50 a share . items.title: AI takes a swing at physics' biggest puzzle
items.description: PLUS: Give jobs to Nod, the personal agent from n8n
items.content: Good morning, AI enthusiasts, and welcome to our 5,002 new readers. The past few months have been all about AI cracking decades-old math problems. Now it’s taking on a physics puzzle unsolved for nearly a century. Stanford physicist Venkatesa Chandrasekaran just proposed a quantum theory of gravity, developed with help from GPT-6 Astra, that could tie together the physics of planets and particles. Some physicists, however, don’t seem impressed. The Rundown: Stanford and OpenAI physicist Venkatesa Chandrasekaran just released an 83-page paper proposing a way to describe gravity with quantum mechanics, saying GPT-6 Astra helped develop several of its calculations and proofs over months and ~400M tokens. The preprint uses the paths that light takes through spacetime to describe gravity at the quantum level, though it only covers empty space and leaves out matter. It claims to avoid the infinities that break standard gravity math, while still agreeing with known results on black holes and Einstein’s general relativity. Sam Altman praised Chandrasekaran for the work and his “confidence and courage to keep pushing on something that others don’t think is possible.”

items.content: Good morning, tech enthusiasts. Hackers spent the past few weeks breaking into banks, crypto platforms, and even supermarket fridges, some with the help of AI. Now the industry is consolidating to fight back, with CrowdStrike buying Zscaler for $43.9B in the biggest cybersecurity deal ever, aimed at protecting every device and connection under one roof. The Rundown: CrowdStrike is paying $43.9B in stock for Zscaler — the largest cybersecurity deal on record — to put the software guarding corporate laptops and the service screening their traffic under one company. CrowdStrike sells endpoint security — the software guarding laptops and phones. Zscaler sells cloud services that replace VPNs and screen traffic for threats. items.title: Claude helps solve math's biggest open problem
items.description: PLUS: Test Gemini 4 Neon on finding billing errors
items.content: Good morning, AI enthusiasts, and welcome to our 8,176 new readers. Few fields have changed more under AI this past year than math. Now, a single Anthropic mathematician and Claude may have solved a problem even the top minds thought was years, if not decades, away. Levent Alpöge says they just proved the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old prime-number puzzle that carries a $1M Millennium Prize and has long been seen as math's most famous open problem. As with AI's other big math wins, not everyone is thrilled. The Rundown: Anthropic’s Levent Alpöge used Claude to crack the Riemann hypothesis, the 167-year-old question often ranked as math's biggest unsolved problem, after ~6 weeks of work, and checkers say it holds up, even as no human fully gets it yet. First posed in 1859, the problem asks whether prime numbers follow a predictable pattern, and the Clay Institute put a $1M “Millennium” prize on solving it in 2000. Alpöge shared the proof only as 17M lines of machine-checkable math, writing that Claude “flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.” The groups behind Lean, the computer language used for verification, certified it on Saturday, saying they have “full confidence” that Alpöge’s proof is correct.
